newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil called up 50 cents before noon expiry.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil called up 50 cents before noon expiry.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were expected to start 50 cents higher on Thursday as the front month ambles towards its noon expiry with only a small delivery anticipated, traders said.
July gas oil closed on Wednesday at $162.50 a tonne, and with thin open interest reported and a little bit of European refinery buying offering support, little dramatic change was forseen.

August Brent IPE futures were called to start five cents higher from their $18.22 a barrel settle, with SIMEX Brent quoted slightly higher but untraded, after a day of being buffeted between news from Baghdad and tightness on the physical crude market.
July gas oil was likely to hold above key support at $162.25 a tonne, brokers said.

August Brent futures closed 16 cents down, pushed lower initially by bearish U.S. stock data and news that Iraq had prepared the aid plan it wants to clear with the United Nations before resuming oil sales.

But European data suggesting lower than forecast product and crude stocks and a tight physical crude market helped prices to recover after they failed to convincingly break through support at around $18.11.
"It was a real yoyo market yesterday, very difficult to read, but I think we are looking a fraction stronger today," said a broker.
